text:
auditor_lee: Hi team — auditor here. We're trying to reconcile an RBAC change (2025-11-12) with KMS access logs around the same window for SOC2 control CC6. Can you provide the exact log slice and a short control mapping (which system log proves which sub-control)?
maya: Hey Lee — can you confirm the org/org-id and service? Is this for inference-prod or a staging tenant?
auditor_lee: inference-prod (org: redwood-main). We need: 1) RBAC change event (who/what/when) 2) KMS decrypt/use events correlated to the same principal 3) any related SSO session start/2FA events.
sam: Copy — I can grab RBAC change from the auth service. Quick Q: do you want the raw DB row export or a human-readable CSV + MD explaining fields?
auditor_lee: Both ideally. CSV for quick review, raw JSON for forensic integrity. Also a small README that maps each column to control language.
kevin: I'll pull KMS CloudTrail entries and its associated access-grant traces. For correlation, what's the acceptable time skew? We have async systems, and some logs add milliseconds — use +/- 5 minutes?
auditor_lee: +/− 5m is fine. If you see any entries outside that window with the same principal, flag them.
lia: I'll add SSO session logs (Okta session start, MFA verified) and link session_id -> principal. That'll help tie the KMS principal back to a human.
maya: Plan: 1) sam exports rbac_changes table rows for 2025-11-12 03:00-04:00 UTC (payload + before/after). 2) kevin exports KMS decrypt/Encrypt/GenerateDataKey events from CloudTrail for same window. 3) lia exports Okta sessions for principals in the RBAC events. 4) I'll produce a control mapping doc (CC6.1 -> RBAC change, CC6.2 -> KMS audit trail, CC6.3 -> session linking).
auditor_lee: Perfect. For the export format: please include checksums for JSON files and a SHA256 for the CSV. Also timestamp each exported file. We'll ingest into the auditor portal.
sam: Working on export now. Example SQL I'll run:```sql
SELECT id, principal, change_type, changed_by, created_at, payload FROM rbac_changes WHERE created_at BETWEEN '2025-11-12T03:00:00Z' AND '2025-11-12T04:00:00Z';
```
kevin: CloudTrail filter I'll use: eventSource:kms.amazonaws.com AND (eventName:Decrypt OR eventName:GenerateDataKey OR eventName:Encrypt) AND eventTime BETWEEN window. I'll include requestParameters.ciphertextBlob hash and userIdentity.principalId.
lia: Okta API calls: /api/v1/logs?since=2025-11-12T02:55:00Z&until=2025-11-12T04:05:00Z&filter=eventType eq "user.session.start" or eventType eq "mfa.challenge.succeed". I'll map the okta.user.id -> SAML subject -> principal.
evidence-bot: export started by sam. job_id: export-9832. ETA ~4m. (reacted :hourglass_flowing_sand:)
ops-bot: Note: production export will read from the read-replica; no locks. Rate limit applied.
sam: Export complete. Files uploaded to internal S3 presign: s3://redwood-audit-exports/6601234321/rbac_changes-20251112.csv (sha256: e3b0c44298...), rbac_changes-20251112.json (sha256: a7f5f35426...).
kevin: KMS logs exported and uploaded: s3://redwood-audit-exports/6601234321/kms_events-20251112.json (sha256: b1946ac924...). Included CloudTrail raw events and a normalized CSV with columns: eventTime, eventName, principalId, requestHash.
lia: Okta logs plus mapping doc uploaded: s3://redwood-audit-exports/6601234321/okta_sessions-20251112.json (sha256: c5d9f3a1...). The mapping table okta_id -> saml_subject -> principal_id.csv included.
maya: Control mapping doc uploaded: s3://redwood-audit-exports/6601234321/control_mapping_CC6.pdf (sha256: d2d2d2d2...). Short summary: CC6.1 (change control) — rbac_changes row proves who made change and before/after; CC6.2 (crypto ops) — CloudTrail KMS events show use and tie to principal_id; CC6.3 (auth proof) — Okta session shows MFA.
auditor_lee: This is great. Two follow-ups: 1) Can you add a short statement about log retention policy and where these exports were pulled from (region + replica)? 2) Any red flags found during triage (unexpected principals, failed decrypts, missing MFA)?
sam: Export note added to README: pulled from read-replica `auth-read.eastus-1`, region eastus-1. Retention policy: system logs retained 365 days in hot storage, 3 years archived.
kevin: No failed decrypts in the window. There was one KMS use from a service principal svc-billing at 03:12:41Z that was not in the RBAC change list — flagged it. Looks like background billing job. I included an annotation in the CSV row: note=background-billing-job.
lia: Okta shows MFA for the human principals. svc-billing is a machine account and has service-key mapping; included that in mapping doc.
auditor_lee: Thanks — please put the flagged svc-billing note in the control mapping as an exception with owner (billing-team) and remediation plan (audit ticket #5481).
maya: Done. Added a row in control_mapping_CC6.csv: exception svc-billing -> owner billing-team -> ticket 5481.
auditor_lee: Final ask: Could you produce a single zipped evidence bundle with checksums and a short manifest (manifest.csv) listing file, sha256, exported_by, export_time, source_host?
sam: Will do. evidence-bot: Created presigned link for bundle: https://presign.redwood-internal/s/6601234321/bundle.tar.gz (expires in 72h).
auditor_lee: Received, downloading. Thanks everyone — I'll follow up if the intake process flags anything. :thumbsup:
maya: Good job team. Leaving this thread open for 24h in case auditor asks for deeper tracebacks.
kevin: If auditor needs raw CloudTrail S3 path let me know — we can schedule transfer to their portal under NDA.
auditor_lee: Appreciate it. One more tiny ask: can you add the playbook snippet you used to run the export in the README so we can reproduce?
sam: Added playbook excerpt to README:```bash
# export rbac changes
pg_dump --table=rbac_changes --data-only --file=rbac_changes-20251112.sql -h auth-read.eastus-1
# normalize
python tools/normalize_rbac_export.py --in rbac_changes-20251112.sql --out rbac_changes-20251112.csv
```
auditor_lee: Perfect. I'll close the loop after ingest. Thanks all.
maya: :white_check_mark:
